subject: Physics
standard_explanation: Gravity is an invisible fundamental pulling force that draws objects toward the center of the Earth. Any object dropped from a height accelerates downward because Earth's mass attracts it. Gravity keeps our feet on the ground and causes falling objects to head toward Earth.
simplified_explanation: Gravity is Earth's giant invisible hug! When you let go of a ball or an apple, gravity gently catches it and pulls it down to the ground. Without gravity, everything would float away into space!
key_points: Gravity is an invisible pulling force from Earth.
When you drop an object, gravity pulls it straight down.
Gravity keeps people, oceans, and trees safely on the ground.
Heavy things and light things both fall toward Earth.
examples: Dropping a basketball and watching it bounce back up and down to the floor.
A leaf tumbling gently from a high tree down to the grass.
misconceptions: Misconception: Heavy objects always fall much faster than light objects in a vacuum. Fact: Gravity pulls all objects downward with the same acceleration when there is no air resistance.
Misconception: There is no gravity when you jump. Fact: Gravity is what brings you safely back down every time you jump.

visual_scenes.title: Apple on the Tree Branch
visual_scenes.description: A bright red apple rests quietly on a tree branch.

visual_scenes.title: Gravity Pulls Downward
visual_scenes.description: The apple snaps free and drops straight toward the grass due to Earth's invisible gravity.
visual_scenes.caption: Step 2: Earth's invisible gravity pulls the apple down to the ground!

visual_scenes.title: Safe on the Earth
visual_scenes.description: The apple rests happily on the grass, held firmly by Earth's gravity.
visual_scenes.caption: Step 3: Gravity holds everything safely on Earth's surface.

Makes it fly up to the Sun
